I'll run LedgerMind's analysis over your intents.
**Verdict: the spending itself is fine — the *authorisations* are the problem.** Risk level: medium.

Your agent has spent **$1.28 total** across 4 payments, all receipted, all to the single merchant each intent was scoped to. No off-allowlist spend, no anomalies. But you've authorised **$67** against that $1.28 of actual use.

**Two things to fix now:**

1. **Withdraw $0.80 from `0xe88b…df16`** (marketing trial, revoked). You funded $1.00, the agent spent $0.20, and the rest is stranded — it's the entirety of your idle capital. Riskless to recover.

2. **Restrict merchants on `0x5682…2f5b`** ("General ops agent – discretionary spend"). This is the one that should bother you: **$10 total cap, $2 per-tx, and an empty allowlist** — meaning the agent can pay *any* address. It has made **zero payments**, so there's no usage history justifying that openness. If you can't name the merchants it needs, just revoke it; you'd lose nothing.

**Two to review this week:**

3. **`0x4e08…bcf4`** (cloud infra autopay) — both payments were $0.49 against a $0.50 per-tx cap, i.e. **98% utilisation twice in a row**. That's a cap sized just under the real invoice, not an agent picking amounts. It will start failing as usage grows. Consider raising per-tx to ~$0.75. Also note it burned **49% of its $2 total cap in a single day**.

4. **`0xb530…7ca7`** (research subscriptions) — $50 authorised, $0.10 spent (0.2% used). That's ~500x headroom. The allowlist is restricted to one merchant so the blast radius is contained, but cutting the total cap to single digits would remove ~$45 of standing exposure with no operational cost.

**Caveat on the data:** every payment falls on a single day (2026-09-13) despite a 90-day window, so there's no real trend or cadence baseline yet — the "weekly" claim on the infra intent isn't verifiable from spend history. Merchant addresses also have no names, so I can't tell you *which* counterparties to allowlist on the ops intent. Data is fresh (indexed block 270,809,814, no indexing errors).

data.headline: Spending itself is small and fully receipted, but $0.80 sits recoverable on a revoked intent and $67 of authorisation is badly mis-shaped — including a $10 intent with an empty merchant allowlist and a cloud-infra intent hitting 98% of its per-tx cap on every payment.

findings.title: Idle capital stranded on revoked trial intent
findings.detail: 0xe88b…df16 was revoked ('Trial ended, tool not adopted') after a single $0.20 payment, but $0.80 of the $1.00 funded remains on the intent. It is unspendable and unrecoverable until withdrawRemainder is called. This is 100% of the reported idle capital in the account.

findings.title: Unrestricted merchant allowlist on the largest active authorisation
findings.detail: 0x5682…2f5b ('General ops agent - discretionary spend') carries a $10 total cap and $2 per-tx cap with merchantAllowlistSize=0 and unrestrictedMerchants=true. It has never paid anyone (0 payments, 0% cap used), so there is no usage evidence justifying open-ended merchant access. If the agent key is compromised, this intent is the widest blast radius in the set — $10 of the $67 authorised, payable to any address in five $2 transactions.
evidence: fundedUsdc 0.3 currently at risk of immediate drain; remaining $9.70 drainable on top-up

findings.title: Cloud infra agent is being throttled by its per-tx cap
findings.detail: Both payments on 0x4e08…bcf4 were $0.49 against a $0.50 per-tx cap — 98% utilisation, twice in a row, to the same merchant 0x1111. That is the signature of a cap sized just under actual invoice size, not of an agent choosing amounts. This is also the only intent with meaningful cap consumption (49% of its $2 total cap burned in one day), so at the current weekly cadence the total cap will bind shortly after the next two payments.
evidence: 0x4e0866d3c7ac1acbd4058cc9a0877193e640bcf4 spentUsdc 0.98 / totalCapUsdc 2 = 49% in a single day

findings.title: Research intent over-authorised by roughly 500x observed spend
findings.detail: 0xb530…7ca7 authorises $50 total with a $5 per-tx cap, but has made one $0.10 payment using 2% of the per-tx cap and 0.2% of the total cap. The allowlist is restricted to one merchant (0x2222), which contains the damage, but the headroom is unjustified by any observed behaviour.
evidence: single payment 0.1 USDC at 2% of perTxCap, merchantAllowlistSize=1

findings.title: Payment hygiene is clean
findings.detail: All four payments carry receipts and each landed with a single merchant per intent, matching each intent's stated purpose. No off-allowlist spend, no merchant concentration anomaly beyond the expected infra vendor. The problem is authorisation shape, not agent behaviour.

actions.rationale: Intent is already revoked and will never spend again; $0.80 of funded USDC is sitting idle and is the entirety of reported idle capital. Withdrawal is riskless and immediate.

A $10 cap with an empty allowlist and zero payment history is the widest unearned exposure in the account. Pin it to the specific merchants the ops agent actually needs; if none can be named, revoke instead — there is no usage to lose.

Two consecutive payments at 98% of the $0.50 per-tx cap indicate the cap is sized just under real invoice size and will start rejecting payments as GPU/storage usage grows. Raise the per-tx cap modestly (e.g. to $0.75) so the weekly autopay does not fail, and pair it with a deliberate total-cap review since 49% of the $2 total burned in one day.

$50 authorised against $0.10 observed spend (0.2% used) is 500x headroom. Cutting the total cap to single digits retains full operating room for subscription payments while removing most of the standing authorisation. Allowlist is already restricted, so this is exposure reduction rather than urgent containment.

dataGaps: The window is stated as 90 days but every payment and every dailySpend row falls on 2026-09-13 — there is no spend history to establish a baseline, trend, or true weekly cadence for the 'weekly' cloud infra intent.
Merchant addresses (0x1111, 0x2222, 0x3333) have no names or categories, so allowlist recommendations for 0x5682 cannot specify which counterparties to permit.

No information on why funded amounts sit far below total caps (e.g. $0.30 funded against a $10 cap on 0x5682) — unclear whether top-ups are automated, which determines how much of the $67 authorised is genuinely drainable today versus only after a funding action.
No agent key custody or rotation data, so the severity of the unrestricted-allowlist exposure on 0x5682 cannot be calibrated.

Receipt flags are boolean only; no indication of receipt content or whether amounts were reconciled against merchant invoices, so the 98% per-tx utilisation cannot be confirmed as genuine invoice size versus agent-side clamping.
